description: Make a scroll-stopping thumbnail from your own video on iPhone: pick the best frame, export it in full quality, add text and upload to YouTube, TikTok or Reels.

card_title: Make a thumbnail from your video on iPhone
excerpt: Find the frame that earns the click, export it sharp, and turn it into a YouTube, TikTok or Reels cover.
lead: The best thumbnail is usually already in your video — a real expression, a real moment. The trick is finding that frame and getting it out sharp enough to survive text, cropping and compression.
quick_answer: Open your video in Video To Photo – Grab Frame, scrub to a sharp, expressive moment, grab two or three options and export the best as PNG. Add big text in any editor (1280 × 720 for YouTube, 9:16 for TikTok and Reels), then upload it as your custom thumbnail or cover.
content_intro:
What makes a thumbnail frame work

  • A clear face or subject — close, sharp and facing the camera.
  • Emotion — surprise, laughter or concentration beats a neutral look.
  • Space for text — a less busy side of the frame where a few words fit.
  • Sharpness — thumbnails are tiny; any blur makes them look amateur.

Thumbnail sizes to aim for

PlatformShapeSize
YouTube16:91280 × 720
YouTube Shorts, TikTok, Instagram Reels9:16 cover1080 × 1920
Instagram grid previewCrops to 1:1 / 4:5Keep the subject centred

A frame from a 1080p or 4K video already exceeds these sizes, so extract the frame from the file rather than taking a screenshot to keep it crisp.
steps_title: How to make a thumbnail from your video on iPhone

steps.name: Open your finished video
steps.text: Share it from Photos to Video To Photo – Grab Frame, or open the app and pick the clip.

steps.name: Grab 3 thumbnail candidates
steps.text: Scrub to strong moments and tap Grab This Frame on each. Expressions change fast, so grab neighbouring frames too.

steps.name: Pick the sharpest
steps.text: Zoom into faces in the preview. Delete anything with motion blur or closed eyes.

steps.name: Export as PNG and add text
steps.text: Export as PNG to keep quality through editing, then add a short headline in your editor and upload it as the custom thumbnail.

content_body:
Full walkthrough: How to make a thumbnail from a video on iPhone.

Upload it as your custom thumbnail

  • YouTube: in the YouTube or YouTube Studio app, edit the video's details and choose a custom thumbnail from your photos. Custom thumbnails require a verified account.
  • TikTok: before posting, tap Edit cover and pick the image or a frame.
  • Instagram Reels: tap Edit cover and add from your camera roll.

Tips that lift click-through

  • Three to five words of text, max.
  • High contrast between subject, text and background.
  • Keep a consistent style across videos so viewers recognise you.
  • Test two frames — swap the thumbnail after a few days and compare.

More ideas in our blog post on creating thumbnails from videos.

faq.q: Can I use a frame from my video as a YouTube thumbnail?
faq.a: Yes. Extract the frame, add text if you like, and upload it as a custom thumbnail. A 1280 × 720 image in JPG or PNG under YouTube's size limit works best.

faq.q: Should I export thumbnails as JPG or PNG?
faq.a: Export the frame as PNG while you edit, so text stays crisp. Save the final thumbnail as JPG if you need a smaller file for upload.

faq.q: Why does my thumbnail look blurry?
faq.a: Usually because it's a screenshot or a frame with motion. Extract the frame from the video file and choose a moment where the subject is still.
